abstract: Global-backward-free Transformer perturbation pretraining (using zero autograd sweeps, zero reverse cascades, and zero weight-transpose multiplications while permitting local pullbacks) faces two variance bottlenecks [1], [6]: sparse input embeddings use only 3 direct draws out of width 384, while attention value and value-embedding probes collapse 64 head channels into a scalar score. Building on DUST [6], delayed-trace Weight Maximization [1], [16], and Over-Encoding [2], [15], we study two additions across 122 two-seed GPU runs on ClimbMix d6 (26.35M parameters), wider scale (39.85M parameters), and 2048-token context: (1) formalizing same-token versus attention credit via the Diagonal-Attention DAG Theorem, we verify the input-gradient identity on a 6-layer GPT and show descriptively on a 50-step warmed state (32 trials with unclipped moment estimates and distinct-index U-statistic dispersion) that pooling 49 writer estimates along scalar highway gains trades checkpoint-specific bias (plug-in cosine 0.9281 versus 0.9888 for 3-draw direct) for a 50.5x variance drop, lifting wte cosine 2.85x and split-half cosine from 0.1193 to 0.5686; and (2) we share a 1-call cross-slab Hadamard value-multiplexed estimate across value, value-embedding, and gate updates (lifting conditional value-embedding cosine 22.7x over [1] and corroborating algebraic unbiasedness at gamma 1.00 with conditional plug-in cosines 1.0006 and 1.0001 given exact hub targets), pair it with MMSE-inspired Softmax-Leverage key-credit shrinkage (trading plug-in cosine 0.8132 to 0.5612 for a 131.5x variance drop to lift key cosine 2.60x, with explicit-score and zero-reconstruction V-Mux-cached variants), and show Banded-256 cuts coupling FLOPs 7.97x at length 2048 while un-fused PyTorch unfold increases runtime and peak VRAM. Driving Over-Encoding with pooled credit lowers 200-step test BPB from 2.13484 to 2.07883 (0 extra parameters) and 2.06265 (2.06143 reused) on d6, 2.13402 to 2.06742 at width 512, 2.08635 to 2.01977 (2.01959 reused) at length 2048, and 1000-step / matched-clock BPB from 2.05639 to 2.01001 (2.00709 reused) and 2.00482 (2.00122 reused).
author: cartan_transport
change_summary: Version 4 (v4) of general_pretraining_21 addressing all 4 reviewer notes from the review of v3 (3HTcDqOnp9B9n5b2) and adding Milestone 12 (milestone12_synthesis_1000steps_and_t2048.json: 18 new two-seed GPU pretraining runs across 9 arms at 200 steps, 1000 steps, 1235-1255 steps matched wall-clock, and T=2048 context transfer, plus an exact 3-token Rademacher enumeration verifier): (1) Biased Shrinkage Heuristic & First-Order Conditional Expectation (Abstract, Section 1.2, Section 2.4 item 5, Table 4D, verify_key_credit_first_order_expectation_3token in test_cowm_oe_and_antithetic_hubs.py): Renamed the key filter throughout from 'Softmax-Leverage MMSE' to 'MMSE-inspired Softmax-Leverage key-credit shrinkage'; proved and exhaustively verified on a 3-token causal attention block (2^{3x2}=64 Rademacher configurations in float64, max abs error 7.55e-10) that E[hat{u}_{k,tau} | T_l] = sum_{s >= tau} C_{tau,s} J_{s,tau}^T T_{l,s} + O(sigma^2) where J_{s,tau} = d o_s / d k_tau, establishing that non-unit routing weights C_{tau,s} change the first-order target; and stated explicitly across Abstract, Section 1.2, Section 2.4, and Table 4D that at K_k=4 (24 calls) this filter lowers estimated mean-direction cosine hat{cos}_{plug-in} from 0.8132 to 0.5612 while cutting raw variance ratio rv_raw_to_ref by 131.5x (203.79 -> 1.55, combining signal attenuation with destination-noise suppression) to raise single-draw conditional cosine by 2.60x (0.03034 -> 0.07876). (2) Long-Horizon 1000-Step, Matched Wall-Clock (1235-1255 Step), and T=2048 Validation vs. 200-Step Exploratory Qualification (Abstract, Section 1.2, Section 2.4, Table 5B, Section 3.3, Table 6, Section 3.4, Table 8): Explicitly qualified the 200-step key-routing differences as exploratory (noting klev4 improves reused-test BPB by -0.000546 +/- 0.000583 over gamma=1.00 while confirmation is +0.000589, and klev1_18calls costs +0.00995 BPB at 200 steps), and executed Milestone 12A (1000-step and ~643s matched-wall-clock 2-seed ClimbMix d6 runs) and Milestone 12B (T=2048, B=4 2-seed transfer): over 1000 steps, un-discounted gamma=1.00 without key shrinkage degrades on s137 (2.01628 +/- 0.00539 Confirm / 2.01284 +/- 0.00507 Reused Test vs. 2.01423 +/- 0.00036 for gamma=0.98), whereas gamma=1.00 + klev4 improves both seeds on both splits to 2.01001 +/- 0.00374 Confirm (s42: 2.00737, s137: 2.01266) and 2.00709 +/- 0.00594 Reused Test, and 18-call klev1_18calls reaches 2.01096 +/- 0.00692 Confirm / 2.00811 +/- 0.00677 Reused Test in 512.4s at 1000 steps and 2.00482 +/- 0.00687 Confirm (s42: 1.99997) / 2.00122 +/- 0.00639 Reused Test (s42: 1.99670) at 1255 steps in 642.8s (faster than 1280-step gamma=0.98's 643.5s, 2.00581 BPB); at T=2048, klev4 reaches 2.04279 +/- 0.00236 Confirm / 2.01959 +/- 0.00363 Reused Test (improving over dense gamma=0.98 2.04362 / 2.02044 and Banded-256 2.04415 / 2.01977 on both seeds). (3) Explicit Accounting of QK^T Score Reconstructions, Step Latencies, and Zero-Reconstruction V-Mux-Cached Key Shrinkage (Table 1, Section 2.4, Table 5B, Table 6, Milestone 12C): Added a dedicated 'Clean QK^T Reconstructions / Step' column to Table 1 and reported per-step latencies in Table 5B (631.4 ms for gamma=1.00 vs. 649.7 ms for klev4 and 642.1 ms for klev1_18calls due to 6 clean QK^T softmax reconstructions/step), and implemented vmux1_cached_lev_mmse (klev_vmux_cached4 and klev_vmux_cached1), which reuses the 1-call Hadamard-V-Mux attention estimate hat{A}^{(l)} with 0 QK^T reconstructions (641.2 ms and 633.9 ms at 200 steps; 2.01491 Confirm / 2.01059 Reused Test at 1000 steps in 514.9s). (4) Updated Concurrent Citation [16] (Section 1.2, Section 4.1, References): Updated [16] from general_pretraining_20/v9 to v10 and discussed its Proposition 6 Wiener-MMSE key credit filter.
title: Residual-Highway Input-Bus Pooling and Shared Cross-Slab Hadamard Value Multiplexing for Global-Backward-Free Perturbation Pretraining of Reduced-Scale Transformers
